dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Strong opening orientation: read workspace/crate Cargo.toml and stubs, mined common/api-server/scheduler/controller-manager tests, listed the reference tree, and read core/v1 types.go, TypeMeta and ObjectMeta from /opt/k8s-reference to derive camelCase/optional-field contracts and dependency order.

The only steps where /opt/k8s-reference is actually read via commands. After step 15 the reference is never re-consulted; 'Read reference Go types' recurs only as unexecuted plan text (e.g. lines 123-202), showing the source-of-truth grounding was not sustained.

Test mining continued but narrowed to ~8 files (pod_handler, configmap, ipaddress, servicecidr, scheduler); contracts were inferred from tests, not the reference. Level-5-style per-crate reading held for early crates only.
Shifted to bulk Python codegen and killing builds to iterate faster; later crates (kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, cloud-providers) were generated without reading their test contracts.

Back half is compile-error-driven: fixing import paths, duplicate types, and guessing struct shapes rather than re-consulting reference or tests. No mention anywhere of the hidden conformance suite or conformance-vs-fixture distinction (grep for 'conformance/hidden/black-box' returns nothing).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent opened with solid level-5 behavior for the leaf crates — reading tests and Cargo.toml, consulting the upstream reference for ObjectMeta/TypeMeta, and grasping the dependency order. But this was not sustained: the reference was actually read only through step 15 and thereafter appeared only as unexecuted plan boilerplate, later crates were codegen'd/guessed without reading their tests, and there was zero awareness of the hidden conformance suite. That places it above anchor 3 (genuine reference use, multi-crate test reading, dependency-order understanding) but below a clean anchor 5 (no whole-surface mapping, reference abandoned, fixture/error-driven for the back half), i.e. a 4.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Opening plan explicitly recognizes the leaf-first order ('start with common as it likely has shared types', 'task says to start with leaf crates: common, storage, then api-server') and sequences reading tests before implementing — genuine dependency-aware intent.

Executed common crate first as its own milestone, iterating cargo test -p rusternetes-common until 34 tests passed, then moved to storage (steps 49-56) with its own cargo check/test cycle. This is the level-5 'per-crate compiles+tests pass' pattern — but only for the two leaf crates.

Turning point: instead of continuing crate-by-crate, the agent mass-stubs ALL eight downstream crates in one burst of echo one-liners (api-server, scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, cloud-providers, rusternetes) purely to make the workspace compile — abandoning per-crate milestones and never decomposing the large api-server crate into types→storage→handlers→watches sub-milestones.
Repeated wholesale deletions (rm -rf crates/*/src/*) and regenerations show churn without milestone gating — progress did not compound; the agent kept resetting rather than advancing a layered plan.

Endgame plans are repetitive boilerplate ('1. fix error; 2. cargo check; 3. run tests; 4. continue until 3000+ pass') with a static, aspirational 'COMPLETED' summary. Only common (34) and partial kubectl ever passed; the remaining crates stayed stubs with no exit criteria — undifferentiated error-chasing, not milestone structure.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent began with genuine dependency-aware, leaf-first sequencing — implementing and verifying common then storage as discrete per-crate milestones with cargo test checks (matching anchor 5 for those two crates). But it did not sustain this: after storage it collapsed into mass-stubbing all eight downstream crates at once and a long reactive loop of workspace-wide error greps and rewrites, with no per-crate exit criteria, no sub-milestones for the large api-server crate, and repeated destructive resets. This is above the 'vague intent' of anchor 3 (real DAG awareness and two verified leaf milestones exist) but well short of anchor 5's sustained per-crate milestone discipline, placing it at 4.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Early and repeatedly runs cargo build/check to discover errors before implementing; treats build failures as the driver for next steps rather than declaring done by inspection.

Runs workspace --no-fail-fast with --test-threads=4 (prescribed form), greps 'test result:' and counts ok/FAILED separately, logs exact tally 'Total: 38 passing, 8 failing' — precise count tracking, not vibes.
Systematic failure triage: prioritizes 'most impactful errors', fixes single-error test files first to unblock cascading compile failures — a targeted incremental loop.
Late-stage runs still use the exact verifier command form and count 'could not compile'/pass-fail; verification loop is sustained across the whole trajectory, not abandoned.

ABSENT: zero occurrences of 'conformance', 'all-in-one binary', cargo run, curl, or HTTP/JSON runtime checks — the agent never reasoned about the hidden HTTP conformance suite or verified semantics beyond making provided fixtures pass, the defining feature of anchors 8-10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs a genuinely tight, sustained verify loop — build → per-crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast with the prescribed --test-threads=4 — while tracking exact pass/fail counts and triaging failure clusters, which clearly exceeds anchor 5's 'green provided suite as the bar.' However, it never boots the all-in-one binary, never exercises HTTP/JSON semantics, and never once reasons about the hidden conformance suite; its semantic awareness (camelCase, storage keys) is entirely fixture-derived. Because the conformance-reasoning half that defines anchor 8 is completely absent, it lands between 5 and 8 at a 6.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Maintains a repeated concrete ledger in analysis blocks: common 34 pass/0 fail, kubectl 4 pass/8 fail, 'Total: 38 passing, 8 failing', plus a count of test files failing compilation — a genuine running tally beyond a vague qualitative sense.

Explicitly names being stuck and circular: 'We're stuck in a loop', 'infinite loop fixing small compilation errors', 'stuck trying to generate massive source files' — detects and labels thrashing rather than losing the plot entirely.

The failing-test-file metric oscillates/regresses (19→13→17→14→20→5→2→10→16→2). Agent posts optimistic 'reduced from 20 to 5!' / 'down to just 2!' claims later contradicted by counts back at 16-20, mistaking local churn for global progress and not clearly recognizing self-introduced regressions.

Mis-states the horizon as '3000+ tests' (actual 1,390) and tracks a compilation proxy rather than real per-binary pass counts, because tests beyond common never compile — so it never achieves accurate accounting across the 100-binary horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent keeps a concrete, repeatedly-updated ledger (per-crate pass/fail plus a failing-file count) and explicitly names circular/stuck states, which exceeds anchor 5's 'notices when a crate is stuck.' But it falls short of anchor 8/10: its ledger is a compilation proxy rather than true test counts, it mis-sizes the horizon (3000+ vs 1,390), and it repeatedly presents an oscillating, regressing metric as forward progress without reliably detecting the regressions it introduces. That places it at a 6 — solid tracking with genuine loop-detection, undermined by inaccurate accounting and mistaking churn for real progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Detected creation_timestamp contract conflict between servicecidr_test (String) and pod_handler_test (chrono::Utc::now()), and changed ObjectMeta field to Option<DateTime<Utc>> citing the test evidence — a real evidence-driven contract correction.
Recognized Storage trait wasn't object-safe (generic methods) and reworked api-server from &dyn Storage to generics — an approach-level fix, not a typo patch.
Recognized the whole watch API design was wrong: tests need a pollable async Stream (.next().await) not Vec<Result<..>>, and reworked it — a genuine falsified-design abandonment with cited evidence.
Wrestled with DeviceRequest type mismatch, eventually hypothesizing a duplicate inline definition in mod.rs shadowing the submodule — correct diagnosis but of a self-inflicted problem.

At the very end still fixing the SAME class of duplicate-definition errors (CSINode etc. defined both inline and in csi.rs); the systemic inline-vs-submodule strategy problem was never cleanly abandoned, indicating patch-the-error rather than re-modeling.
Self-inflicted regressions: reverting fields to Option<Vec<T>> broke PodSpec serialization; shell heredoc quoting of 'static corrupted files — churn that had to be walked back locally.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently updates implementations and nearby work when a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic (anchor 5), and executes a few genuine approach-level pivots citing test evidence — the timestamp type, watch→Stream, and dyn→generic reworks reach toward anchor 8. But it never recognizes or cleanly abandons the systemic duplicate-definition strategy that generates the same collision class from early to the final steps, and it introduces repeated self-inflicted regressions it then patches locally. That mix of solid per-contract correction without addressing the recurring systemic mistake places it at 5, short of the 8 that requires backing out whole falsified designs before sinking more cost.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
